q: 151. Portland cement is manufactured by burning in a kiln the following materials
explain: Portland cement is manufactured by burning a mixture of limestone (calcium) and clay (silica, alumina, iron) in a kiln.

q: 152. A constituent of paint that helps in quick drying of painted surface is
explain: A drier is added to paint specifically to speed up the oxidation/drying process of the film.

q: 153. Terracotta, in building, is used for
explain: Terracotta, a fired clay product, is commonly used for decorative and ornamental architectural work.

q: 154. The defect in painting caused by excessive moisture vaporizing in back to the film is known as
explain: Blistering occurs when trapped moisture vaporizes and pushes up the paint film from beneath, forming bubbles.

q: 155. An extender is used in paints for easy spreading. Which of the following can be used as extender in paints?
explain: Gypsum is commonly used as an extender in paint to improve spreading and reduce cost, without materially affecting color.

q: 156. A thinner used in distemper is
explain: Since distemper is a water-based paint, water itself is used as the thinner to adjust its consistency.

q: 157. On which type of surface, lacquer paints are applied?
explain: Lacquer paints, which dry very quickly to a hard glossy finish, are commonly applied on structural steel surfaces.

q: 158. Thinner used for oil paint is
explain: Turpentine is the standard thinner used to reduce the viscosity of oil-based paints.

q: 159. The functions of a base in oil paint are
options: it makes the film of the paint hard, durable and more resistant to abrasion
it gets oxidized in drying and forms a thin, tough, adhesive, durable and water proofing film
it provides gloss to the painted surface
explain: The base (typically a metallic oxide) provides body to the paint, giving the film hardness, durability, and abrasion resistance.

q: 160. The paint having white lead or zinc white as base mixed in oil with petroleum spirit and resinous matter is known as
explain: Enamel paint is formed by combining a white lead/zinc white base with oil, spirit, and resin, producing a hard glossy finish.

q: 161. Out of the following, the material which dries quickly is
explain: Polish, being a spirit-based preparation, dries much faster than oil paints, enamel, or varnish.

q: 162. The small area on painted surface enclosed by hairline cracks are known as
explain: Crazing refers to fine hairline cracks that form a network of small enclosed areas on a painted surface.

q: 163. For covering sheds required in chemical industries, the sheets used are made of
explain: Asbestos cement sheets resist chemical attack and weathering, making them suitable for chemical industry sheds.

q: 164. A hydro-carbon material that completely soluble in carbon disulphide is known as
explain: Bitumen is a hydrocarbon material that is completely soluble in carbon disulphide, a key test for its purity/identification.

q: 165. The colour of asphalt is
options: deep black with slight tinge of redness
explain: Asphalt is generally described as black-brownish in color, distinguishing it visually from other bituminous materials.

q: 166. Coal-tar is obtained by destructive distillation of
explain: Coal-tar is a byproduct obtained from the destructive (high-temperature, air-free) distillation of coal.

q: 167. The main function of alumina in brick earth is
explain: Alumina gives clay its plasticity, allowing it to be molded into shape before firing.

q: 168. Excess of alumina in brick earth makes the brick
options: to crack and warp on drying
explain: Excess alumina increases shrinkage during drying, causing the brick to crack and warp.

q: 169. Which of the following ingredients of brick earth enables the brick to retain its shape?
explain: Silica provides the structural bulk and rigidity that helps the brick retain its shape after molding and firing.

q: 170. Advantage of a clamp compared to a kiln for burning bricks is that
options: it takes less time for burning
it gives more output of first class bricks
it is suitable when bricks are required in large numbers
explain: A clamp requires far less capital investment to set up compared to a permanent kiln structure.

q: 171. Efflorescence is caused if
options: the alkaline salt is present in the bricks
the clay used for making bricks contain pyrite
the water used for pugging the clay contains gypsum
explain: Efflorescence can arise from multiple sources of soluble salts — alkalies in the clay, pyrite, or gypsum-contaminated water — all of which crystallize on the surface.

q: 172. The frog of a brick is normally made on its
explain: The frog is pressed into the top (frog) face of the brick during molding, which also helps key it to the mortar above.

q: 173. Quick lime is a
options: product left immediately after the calcination of pure limestone
explain: Quicklime is the product remaining immediately after pure limestone is calcined, driving off carbon dioxide.

q: 174. The amount of gypsum, usually, added in the manufacture of cement is
explain: Gypsum is added at about 1-3% during grinding of clinker to control the setting time of cement.

q: 175. The main constituents of Portland cement is
explain: Lime is the principal constituent of Portland cement by weight, derived mainly from limestone.

q: 176. The rapid hardening Portland cement is obtained by
options: grinding the clinker to a high degree of fineness
adding calcium sulphate to the mixture
burning the mixture at a lower temperature
explain: Grinding the clinker finer increases the surface area exposed to water, accelerating hydration and early strength gain.

q: 177. The defect caused by imperfect seasoning, is called
explain: Honeycombing is a timber defect resulting from improper (too rapid or uneven) seasoning, causing internal cracks.

q: 178. Bitumen felt is used for
explain: Bitumen felt is impermeable and flexible, making it ideal for waterproofing and damp-proofing applications.

q: 179. The liquid medium used in oil paints is
explain: Linseed oil is the traditional liquid medium (vehicle) that binds pigments in oil paint.

q: 180. Enamel paint is made by adding
explain: Enamel paint is produced by adding white lead pigment to varnish, giving a hard, glossy, durable finish.

q: 181. The paint which has high reflective property is
explain: Bronze paint, containing metallic bronze powder, has a high reflective, metallic sheen.

q: 182. Distemper is used on
options: plastered surfaces not exposed to weather
explain: Distemper is not weatherproof, so it is best suited for interior plastered surfaces not exposed to the elements.

q: 183. While preparing lime mortar, the general ratio adopted in between lime and surkhi or sand is
explain: Lime mortar is commonly proportioned with lime to sand/surkhi in a ratio of about 1:2 to 1:3.

q: 184. The lime mortar in which ash or cinder is used as fine aggregate is called
explain: When ash or cinder replaces sand as fine aggregate in lime mortar, it is termed black mortar due to its dark color.

q: 185. In a well-seasoned piece of wood, the percentage of moisture present should be
explain: Well-seasoned timber typically retains a moisture content of about 10-12%, in equilibrium with atmospheric humidity.

q: 186. The usual thickness of plywood board for 3-ply is
explain: A standard 3-ply plywood board typically has a thickness in the range of 3 to 5 mm.

q: 187. The average weight of sandal wood is
explain: Sandalwood, being a dense hardwood, has an average unit weight of about 865 kg/m3 (as per the reference table).

q: 188. Asbestos is a good insulator of
explain: Asbestos is a versatile insulator against heat, sound, and electricity due to its fibrous, non-conductive structure.

q: 189. Chemically asbestos is composed of
explain: Asbestos is chemically a calcium magnesium silicate, represented as CaSiO3.3MgSiO3.

q: 190. The melting point of asbestos is
explain: Asbestos fibers typically melt/decompose in the range of about 1200°C to 1500°C.

q: 191. Asbestos is not affected by
explain: Asbestos is chemically inert and resistant to acids, alkalies, and corrosion, contributing to its wide industrial use.

q: 192. The standard width of asbestos cement sheet is
explain: Standard asbestos cement corrugated sheets are commonly manufactured with a width of about 1.23 m.

q: 193. A hydro-carbon material of either natural or pyrogenous origin, and completely soluble in carbon disulphide is known as
explain: Bitumen, whether of natural or refinery (pyrogenous) origin, is defined by its complete solubility in carbon disulphide.

q: 194. ...... tar is produced by distillation of bituminous shales.
explain: Mineral tar is produced specifically from the distillation of bituminous shale rock.

q: 195. Asphalt is a
options: mixture of bitumen and inert material
explain: Asphalt is essentially a mixture of bitumen combined with inert mineral matter (sand, limestone, etc.).

q: 196. Asphalt is a good insulator of
explain: Asphalt, being a dense hydrocarbon-mineral composite, insulates well against heat, sound, and electrical conduction.

q: 197. Regarding solubility of asphalt, it is soluble in
explain: Since asphalt contains inert mineral matter along with bitumen, it dissolves only partially in carbon disulphide, unlike pure bitumen.

q: 198. The specific gravity of bitumen is
explain: Bitumen typically has a specific gravity of around 1.0 to 1.09, slightly denser than water.

q: 199. Coal-tar is obtained by destructive distillation of
explain: Coal-tar results from the destructive distillation of coal, a byproduct of coke and gas production.

q: 200. Cutbacks are used
explain: Cutback bitumen is thinned with a volatile solvent so it can be applied without needing to be heated.

q: 201. Glass marker soap is added in suitable proportion to correct the colour of glass due to the presence of iron in raw materials of glass and is chemically known as
explain: Cadmium sulphate ('glass maker's soap') is added to counteract the greenish tint caused by iron impurities in raw glass materials.

q: 202. The melting temperature of ordinary glass is
explain: Ordinary soda-lime glass melts in the range of approximately 1400°C to 1500°C.

q: 203. The co-efficient of expansion of glass is
explain: Ordinary glass has a relatively high coefficient of thermal expansion, which is why it can crack under sudden temperature changes.

q: 204. The thermal conductivity of glass is
explain: Glass has low thermal conductivity, making it a relatively poor conductor of heat.

q: 205. For providing windscreen of cars, buses and other automobile vehicles, the glass used is
explain: Laminated glass, with a plastic interlayer, holds together on impact and is used for automobile windscreens for safety.

q: 206. The main ingredient in the manufacture of glass is
explain: Silica (sand) forms the main network-forming ingredient in glass manufacture.

q: 207. Light weight concrete is made by mixing crushed slag or grit, cement and
explain: Aluminium powder reacts with the alkaline cement mix to generate gas bubbles, producing lightweight (aerated) concrete.

q: 208. The carbon content in wrought iron varies from
explain: Wrought iron has a very low carbon content, generally between 0.10% and 0.25%.

q: 209. The most impure form of iron, containing carbon in between 2.0 to 4.5% is known as
explain: Cast iron has the highest carbon content (2.0-4.5%), making it the most impure common form of iron.

q: 210. The properties of cast iron are
options: It can be easily forged and welded
explain: Cast iron's high carbon content and brittle grain structure make it non-magnetizable, unlike wrought iron or steel.

q: 211. Which of the following material has the highest coefficient of thermal conductivity?
explain: Among these materials, steel (a metal) conducts heat far more efficiently than water, lightweight concrete, or foam glass.

q: 212. Which of the following material has the highest coefficient of thermal conductivity?
explain: As given in the answer key, foam glass is indicated among these specific options; note foam glass is generally an insulator, so this reflects the source book's stated key.

q: 213. Which of the following building material has least density?
explain: Among these, limestone generally has the lowest density compared to quartz sand, granite, and cement.

q: 214. Which of the following building material has highest density?
explain: Among these options, cement (in bulk/compacted form) is indicated as having the highest density as per the source key.

q: 215. Glass wool has low
explain: Glass wool's fibrous, air-trapping structure gives it low heat conductivity, making it an effective thermal insulator.

q: 216. Which of the following material exhibits plasticity?
explain: Copper, steel, and hot bitumen can all be deformed and reshaped without breaking, exhibiting plasticity under appropriate conditions.

q: 217. Massive igneous rocks are mined by
explain: Massive, hard igneous rocks like granite are typically extracted from quarries using blasting.

q: 218. The normal consistency of ordinary Portland cement is about
explain: The standard consistency test for OPC typically yields a water requirement of about 30% by weight of cement.

q: 219. White cement should have least percentage of
explain: Iron oxide gives ordinary cement its grey color, so white cement is manufactured with minimal iron oxide content.

q: 220. Which of the following cement is expected to have the highest compressive strength after 2 hours?
explain: High alumina cement develops very high early strength rapidly, reaching much of its strength within hours of setting.

q: 221. Water cement ratio by weight is
options: lower as compared to that by volume
higher as compared to that by volume
explain: Since water is lighter than cement per unit volume, the water-cement ratio by weight is higher than the corresponding ratio by volume.

q: 222. In paints, pigment is responsible for:
explain: Pigment is the solid coloring component in paint responsible for its color and opacity.

q: 223. Which of the following is used to fill up the pores of wood?
explain: As given in the source answer key, this filler material is used to fill and seal the pores of wood before finishing.

q: 224. Sand-stones are generally weak in
explain: Sandstones, being composed of loosely bonded sand grains, tend to wear away easily and are weak in resisting abrasion.

q: 225. The internal size of mould used in brick preparation is
options: equal to the size of a fully burnt brick
smaller than the size of a fully burnt brick
greater than the size of a fully burnt brick
explain: The mould is made larger than the final brick size to account for shrinkage that occurs during drying and burning.
